note: Every way Indian governments raise money, grouped by what is taxed. 'node' links a tax to its flow in money/flows.json (diagram:node). Levels: union, state, local. Descriptions give the general pattern; rates and details change, so each entry links to its legal basis.

categories.property: Taxes on property, land and transactions

taxes.name: Income tax on individuals, families and firms
taxes.who_pays: Individuals, Hindu undivided families, partnership firms and other non-company taxpayers.
taxes.who_bears: Mostly the earner. Employers deduct it from salaries at source (TDS), which makes it the nearest thing India has to a payroll tax; banks and others deduct it on interest, rent and other payments.
taxes.collected_by: Income Tax Department (Central Board of Direct Taxes)
taxes.shared_with_states: Yes, through the divisible pool, except cesses and surcharges.
taxes.basis: Income-tax Act, 2025 (from 1 April 2026; earlier the Income-tax Act, 1961); Article 270

taxes.name: Corporation tax
taxes.who_pays: Companies, on profits.
taxes.who_bears: Shared in some mix between shareholders, workers and customers; economists disagree on the split.
taxes.collected_by: Income Tax Department (Central Board of Direct Taxes)
taxes.shared_with_states: Yes, through the divisible pool.
taxes.basis: Income-tax Act, 2025; Article 270

taxes.name: Securities transaction tax
taxes.who_pays: Buyers and sellers of listed shares, derivatives and equity mutual fund units, collected by the stock exchange or fund.
taxes.collected_by: Stock exchanges and mutual funds, for the Income Tax Department
taxes.shared_with_states: Yes.
taxes.basis: Finance (No. 2) Act, 2004, Chapter VII

taxes.name: Cesses and surcharges
taxes.who_pays: Added on top of other Union taxes: for example the 4% health and education cess on income tax, surcharges on high incomes, and cesses on fuel and imports.
taxes.collected_by: The department collecting the underlying tax
taxes.shared_with_states: No. Cesses and surcharges are kept out of the divisible pool, so the Union keeps all of them.
taxes.basis: Articles 270 and 271; annual Finance Acts

taxes.name: Employees' Provident Fund and pension contributions
taxes.who_pays: Employer and employee, each generally 12% of basic wages, in establishments with 20 or more workers; part of the employer's share goes to the Employees' Pension Scheme.
taxes.who_bears: Largely workers, through lower take-home or cost-to-company pay.
taxes.collected_by: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation
taxes.shared_with_states: Not a tax: it is saved in members' accounts and paid out as provident fund and pension, outside the Budget.
taxes.basis: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, now under the Code on Social Security, 2020

taxes.name: Employees' State Insurance contributions
taxes.who_pays: Employer 3.25% and employee 0.75% of wages, for workers earning up to ₹21,000 a month in covered establishments.
taxes.who_bears: Largely workers and employers in covered firms.
taxes.collected_by: Employees' State Insurance Corporation
taxes.shared_with_states: Not a tax: it pays for ESI hospitals and sickness, maternity and injury benefits, outside the Budget. States run many ESI hospitals.
taxes.basis: Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948, now under the Code on Social Security, 2020

taxes.name: Professional tax
taxes.who_pays: Salaried employees (deducted by the employer) and professionals, traders and businesses, in states that levy it.
taxes.who_bears: The earner. The Constitution caps it at ₹2,500 a year per person.
taxes.collected_by: State commercial tax departments; in some states local bodies
taxes.shared_with_states: State or local revenue.
taxes.basis: Article 276; state professional tax Acts

taxes.name: Construction workers' welfare cess
taxes.who_pays: Builders and employers in construction, as a percentage (usually 1%) of the cost of construction.
taxes.who_bears: Buyers and users of buildings, through construction costs.
taxes.collected_by: State Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Boards
taxes.shared_with_states: Held by state welfare boards for registered construction workers, outside the Budget.
taxes.basis: Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act, 1996, now under the Code on Social Security, 2020

taxes.name: Central GST
taxes.who_pays: Businesses charge it on sales within a state and claim credit for GST paid on their inputs.
taxes.collected_by: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs; rates set by the GST Council
taxes.shared_with_states: Yes, through the divisible pool (on top of the separate SGST).
taxes.basis: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017; Articles 246A and 279A

taxes.name: State GST
taxes.who_pays: Charged alongside CGST, at the same rate, on sales within a state.
taxes.collected_by: State tax departments; rates set by the GST Council, where the Union has a third of the vote and states two-thirds
taxes.shared_with_states: State revenue. The largest single source of states' own tax (44% in 2025-26).
taxes.basis: State GST Acts, 2017; Article 246A

taxes.name: Integrated GST
taxes.who_pays: Charged on sales between states and on imports.
taxes.collected_by: The Union, which then settles the state share with the state where the goods or services are consumed
taxes.shared_with_states: Split between the Union and the consuming state.
taxes.basis: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017; Article 269A

taxes.name: GST compensation cess
taxes.who_pays: Charged on luxury and 'sin' goods such as tobacco, cars and aerated drinks.
taxes.collected_by: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
taxes.shared_with_states: Used to compensate states for lost revenue after GST, then to repay loans taken for that; no collections are budgeted for 2026-27.
taxes.basis: GST (Compensation to States) Act, 2017

taxes.name: Union excise duties
taxes.who_pays: Manufacturers and refiners of petrol, diesel, tobacco and a few other goods outside or on top of GST.
taxes.collected_by: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
taxes.shared_with_states: Only the basic duty; a large part of fuel excise is levied as cess and kept by the Union.
taxes.basis: Central Excise Act, 1944; Seventh Schedule, Union List entry 84

taxes.name: Sales tax / VAT on fuel and alcohol
taxes.who_pays: Sellers of petrol, diesel, aviation fuel, natural gas and alcohol for drinking, which remain outside GST.
taxes.who_bears: Buyers. Each state sets its own rate, which is why fuel prices differ between states.
taxes.collected_by: State commercial tax departments
taxes.shared_with_states: State revenue (20% of states' own tax).
taxes.basis: State VAT / sales tax Acts; Seventh Schedule, State List entry 54

taxes.name: State excise on alcohol
taxes.who_pays: Makers and sellers of alcohol, as duty and licence fees.
taxes.collected_by: State excise departments
taxes.shared_with_states: State revenue (14% of states' own tax); close to nothing in states with prohibition.
taxes.basis: State excise Acts; Seventh Schedule, State List entry 51

taxes.name: Electricity duty
taxes.who_pays: Electricity consumers, on their bills.
taxes.collected_by: Distribution companies, for the state
taxes.shared_with_states: State revenue.
taxes.basis: State electricity duty Acts; State List entry 53

taxes.name: Entertainment tax
taxes.who_pays: Organisers of entertainment and amusements.
taxes.collected_by: Local bodies, where states allow it
taxes.shared_with_states: Mostly folded into GST in 2017; local bodies can still levy it in some states.
taxes.basis: State List entry 62, as amended by the 101st Amendment

taxes.name: Customs duties
taxes.who_pays: Importers: basic customs duty, the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess and the Social Welfare Surcharge. Imports also carry IGST.
taxes.who_bears: Buyers of imported goods and of goods made with imported inputs; also protects domestic producers.
taxes.collected_by: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
taxes.shared_with_states: Basic duty yes; cesses and surcharges no.
taxes.basis: Customs Act, 1962; Customs Tariff Act, 1975

taxes.name: Stamp duty and registration fees
taxes.who_pays: Buyers of property and parties to leases, mortgages and other legal documents, when the document is registered.
taxes.who_bears: Property buyers. High rates encourage under-declaring the price.
taxes.collected_by: State registration departments (Inspector General of Registration and Stamps; sub-registrars)
taxes.shared_with_states: State revenue (12% of states' own tax). Some states pass a surcharge to municipalities.
taxes.basis: Indian Stamp Act, 1899 and state amendments; Registration Act, 1908

taxes.name: Property tax
taxes.who_pays: Owners (and sometimes occupiers) of buildings and land in municipal and panchayat areas.
taxes.collected_by: Municipal corporations, councils and gram panchayats
taxes.shared_with_states: Local revenue; the main tax local bodies raise themselves.
taxes.basis: State municipal and panchayat Acts; State List entry 49

taxes.name: Land revenue
taxes.who_pays: Holders of agricultural land.
taxes.who_bears: Landholders. Small today; many states have abolished or waived it for small farmers.
taxes.collected_by: State revenue departments (tehsildars and patwaris)
taxes.shared_with_states: State revenue.
taxes.basis: State land revenue codes; State List entry 45

taxes.name: Motor vehicle tax
taxes.who_pays: Vehicle owners, usually once at registration (road tax), plus permit and registration fees.
taxes.collected_by: State transport departments (regional transport offices)
taxes.shared_with_states: State revenue.
taxes.basis: State motor vehicles taxation Acts; State List entry 57

taxes.name: Development charges, premiums and building fees
taxes.who_pays: Builders and landowners, for building permission, extra floor space (premium FSI), change of land use and betterment.
taxes.collected_by: Municipal corporations and development authorities
taxes.shared_with_states: Local or development authority revenue.
taxes.basis: State town planning and municipal Acts

taxes.name: Mining royalties and auction premiums
taxes.who_pays: Holders of mining leases: royalty at rates set by the Union, and the premium they bid when mineral blocks are auctioned.
taxes.who_bears: Mine operators and, through prices, buyers of minerals.
taxes.collected_by: State mining departments
taxes.shared_with_states: State revenue; a large share of non-tax income in mineral-rich states.
taxes.basis: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957

taxes.name: Spectrum and other auction payments
taxes.who_pays: Telecom operators and others winning auctions for spectrum and other rights, plus licence fees.
taxes.collected_by: Department of Telecommunications and other ministries
taxes.shared_with_states: Union non-tax revenue.
taxes.basis: Telecommunications Act, 2023

taxes.name: Reserve Bank surplus and public-company dividends
taxes.who_pays: The Reserve Bank, which transfers its surplus to the Union, and public-sector companies owned by the Union or a state.
taxes.who_bears: Ultimately the users and customers of those institutions.
taxes.collected_by: Ministry of Finance (Department of Investment and Public Asset Management for dividends)
taxes.shared_with_states: Union dividends go to the Union; state companies pay their state.
taxes.basis: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, section 47; Companies Act, 2013

taxes.name: Fees, user charges and fines
taxes.who_pays: Users of public services and licences: tolls, water and sewer charges, court fees, passport and licence fees, liquor licences, fines and penalties.
taxes.collected_by: The department or body providing the service
taxes.shared_with_states: Each level keeps its own.
taxes.basis: Various Acts and rules

taxes.name: Selling stakes and leasing assets
taxes.who_pays: Investors buying government stakes in public companies, and firms leasing public assets such as roads, ports and pipelines (asset monetisation).
taxes.who_bears: Not a tax: the government gives up an asset or its future income in exchange.
taxes.collected_by: Department of Investment and Public Asset Management
taxes.shared_with_states: Union capital receipt.
taxes.basis: Executive policy; the proceeds go to the Consolidated Fund

taxes.name: Government bonds and treasury bills
taxes.who_pays: Lenders: banks, insurers, pension and provident funds, mutual funds, foreign investors and the Reserve Bank in the secondary market. States borrow through state development loans.
taxes.who_bears: Future taxpayers, who pay the interest and principal.
taxes.collected_by: The Reserve Bank, which runs the auctions as debt manager for the Union and states
taxes.shared_with_states: Each government borrows for itself; states need Union consent while they owe it money (Article 293).
taxes.basis: Articles 292 and 293; Government Securities Act, 2006

taxes.name: Small savings
taxes.who_pays: Households saving in the Public Provident Fund, post office deposits, National Savings Certificates, Sukanya Samriddhi and similar schemes.
taxes.who_bears: Future taxpayers; savers earn interest set by the government each quarter.
taxes.collected_by: Post offices and banks, into the National Small Savings Fund
taxes.shared_with_states: Mostly lent to the Union.
taxes.basis: Government Savings Promotion Act, 1873 and scheme rules

taxes.name: Municipal bonds
taxes.who_pays: Investors in bonds issued by municipal corporations, usually for water, sewerage or roads.
taxes.collected_by: The issuing municipal corporation
taxes.shared_with_states: Local; requires state permission.
taxes.basis: SEBI (Issue and Listing of Municipal Debt Securities) Regulations, 2015

taxes.name: States' share of Union taxes
taxes.who_pays: The Union, from the divisible pool of its taxes.
taxes.collected_by: Distributed by the Union among states in shares set by the Finance Commission
taxes.shared_with_states: This is the sharing. Untied: states decide how to spend it.
taxes.basis: Articles 270 and 280

taxes.name: Grants and scheme transfers
taxes.who_pays: The Union (Finance Commission grants, centrally sponsored schemes, loans for capital investment) and states (transfers to local bodies recommended by State Finance Commissions).
taxes.collected_by: Released by the paying government's ministries
taxes.shared_with_states: Often tied to a purpose and to matching money from the receiving government.
taxes.basis: Articles 275, 282, 243-I and 243Y
